markers.reading: Kenzo alone steps off the road to the murky pool and sees painful reflected faces.

evidence.quote:
DM: ... walking, it's like 8:00 at night, um, uh, you pass again, um, a place where, um, a stream seems to flow like on the right side, or sorry, on the left side now 'cause the east seems to s- s- flow close to the, very close to the, the, um, the road.

Delwath: Does the, does the forest keep going up the mountain or-

DM: About halfway up the mountain.

Delwath: Okay. So we're still in the forest.

DM: You're still in the... You haven't hit the part where it spirals yet. When-

Kenzo: And is the stream—and the—is the stream flowing up or down?

DM: Down, but it's stopped. Like it's stopped. You can see it flowing and it stops. And by the side of the, by the side of the road, there's this big pool which the stream flows into, but doesn't exit from.

DM: Um, so you, you walk, you walk over to the pool, um, and as you get closer, you see that the, um, the water is kind of murky and filled with like debris. And there's two stones that are sort of standing next to it, like sort of an entryway to a little viewing area over the pool that are actually cracked. One has fallen in half and part of the stone has, um, fallen into the pool itself. And you can see staring out at you from the pool, like the reflections of people with hollow eyes, their faces contorted in pain. Make a wisdom saving throw.

Unknown: Everybody or just-

DM: Just Kenzo. He's the only one who's—

Delwath: [laughs] Well, I don't know. I was thinking we might have all followed him, but I guess not. [laughs] Thanks for being the, um, guinea pig, Kenzo.

DM: You feel a bit uneasy, but nothing bad happens to you.

Kenzo: 24. Wait, sorry. So I see the reflections of these, these like, like tortured souls or whatever in the thing, but there's no... It's—I'm just seeing their reflections.

DM: You're just seeing the reflections. There's nothing standing around the pool.

Kenzo: Do I sense anything standing around the pool?

DM: Nope.

Kenzo: Um, do I have the heebie-jeebies?

DM: Yeah, a little bit.

Kenzo: Did I have the heebie-jeebies before?

DM: No. I mean, it's a creepy image, right? It's like people who died in pain looking back up at you and kind of screaming at you.

Delwath: But they're not underwater looking up, they're reflections?

Unknown: Is it-

DM: They seem like they're reflections, yeah.

Kenzo: Do they look like they're... So they don't look like they're trapped in there. They look like they're standing around the pool, but I just can't see them?

DM: Exactly. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

Kenzo: And, uh, do they look like they were, um, like what, what was the way in which they died? Were they, do they like have like battle wounds and stuff, or do they look like sickly, um-

DM: Sickly.

Kenzo: Almost as though like a demonic red mist may have—

DM: Kind of something like that, yes.

markers.reading: The group continues another mile or so along the forest road to the next roadside pool, about two miles straight from the summit.

evidence.quote:
Kenzo: I don't know. I'll, I'll touch the water later.

DM: Okay. [laughs] So you ke- you keep going and, and you're now-

Unknown: We'll get that on the way back.

DM: ... another-

Kenzo: All right. I will though.

DM: ... um, it's another, uh, mile or so as you, the pa—the road begins to like go slightly up, um, and you can see about, um, half a mile ahead is the place where it curved that you can't—you couldn't see beyond. Kenzo: Right. Are we about two miles away yet?

DM: Um, at this point, yeah. I mean, the, the road is longer than two miles from here, but the-

Unknown: Straight off is two miles.

DM: ... straight off is about two miles, yeah.

markers.reading: Clairvoyance above the bell tower reveals the broken light, the courtyard and the eight intact temples without signs of substantial inhabitation.

evidence.quote: Seeker: Um, yeah, so I'll use one glove charge and cast—what level is clairvoyance? Third, one, third level slot. Oh, second level slot. All right. And I'm gonna place the sensor... We don't really know anything about the layout of the buildings though, do we?

Seeker: I, I think actually I'm gonna put it up high-

Kenzo: I like that.

Seeker: ... near the bell tower-

Kenzo: I like that.

Seeker: ... so I can look, I can inspect the crystal structure and also see down into the courtyard and through any windows.

Kenzo: That, that's great.

DM: All right.

DM: So you see, um, this looks like—so there's the bell tower. The, the, the bell is intact.

Unknown: Mm-hmm.

DM: Um, but this, the structure that stands on top of it looks like it once was like a, like a giant sort of crystalline light that's now broken and cracked. Like you can see mirrors, like it was clearly...

Unknown: It's like a lighthouse almost.

DM: But it would've sh- shown somehow, probably magic, but it's like clearly sort of also constructed, right? It's not just a crystal that glows magically, right? It's like-

Unknown: A mechanism.

DM: ... a mechanism, but the mechanism is destroyed or cracked. Um, the bell is intact, and then looking down, the courtyard is in pretty good shape, right? Like it's paved, um, and-

DM: ... and it's [laughs], and there's eight, so there's eight temples that surround the courtyard, each one with a separate statue of the, of the eight gods of Mos Numena. No sign of anything there, just the moonlight shining over the stones.

Unknown: No lights?

DM: No lights, no torches, no fires, no movement, no weird creepy shadows, no dragons.

Seeker: Try sound for a minute just to see.

DM: You hear the sort of murmur of the wind.

Seeker: All's qui- all's quiet here.

Kenzo: Hmm. Hmm.

Seeker: It seems we should approach quietly.

Kenzo: Do we, um...

Seeker: Oh, signs of just like recent foot traffic, like any wear on the stones or like leaves piled and...

DM: Make a investigation check.

Seeker: So [die rolling] 18.

Unknown: [laughs]

Seeker: Oh, three.

DM: Is it—your perspective is a little bit high to see any, like, careful detail because the... I mean, the bell tower goes up fairly tall, right?

Seeker: Mm. Oh, yeah. I'm high up.

DM: And you're up above the bell tower, so it's hard to make out any obvious details. But it definitely doesn't seem to be destroyed in the same way that, like, the town, the port town was destroyed. Like, there's not... The, the temples are all intact.

Seeker: Mm.

DM: Like, their roofs, they're, like, not... And there's no... There's definitely not signs of, you know, a large group of something living here, right? Like, there's no-

Wellby: No trash. There's no-

DM: There's no trash. There's no... Yeah, there's no, like, scraps of food. There's no, like, clothes hanging out to dry. There's no, like, signs of substantial inhabitation. But if, like, one dragonet is walking around, like, they wouldn't really leave enough right behind for you to notice-

Seeker: Mm.

DM: ... from this high up.

Seeker: [sighs] Hmm. Well, that's what we get from clairvoyance, I guess.

markers.reading: The party remains at the forest-road stop while waiting for the messenger and taking a short rest.

evidence.quote:
Kenzo: Should we short rest anyways while we wait?

Delwath: I mean, that I was just thinking maybe we should short rest while we're waiting.

Kenzo: That'd be great. That'll get all my ki back.

DM: Okay. Send it off. Short rest. Yes. No response comes.
DM: It's not a familiar. It's just like a spirit messenger. So you finish your short rest uneventfully.

markers.reading: During the same rest, Delwath scries the elder rigging a boulder trap in the Temple of the Sibyl.

evidence.quote:
DM: ... a very, um, elderly, um, dragonet. Same kind of creature as before. Their skin is almost a light gray. It seems like all color has faded from their skin. There's, like, a few faint little traces of purple that you can see.

Kenzo: Mm.

DM: And they're currently walking slowly around the inside of a temple. You can't tell which one it is from the inside, and seem to be in the process of rigging some kind of trap to drop from the ceiling on whoever enters the temple.

Kenzo: [laughs]

Delwath: Yeah. What, like, I'm gonna study the trap for a little bit. What's the trigger mechanism? Is it obvious?

DM: Um, he hasn't gotten to the trigger mechanism yet.

Delwath: Oh, okay.

DM: Right now he seems to be just struggling with some pulleys and rope to, like, lift... Like, it looks like a pretty substantial-

Delwath: Right.

DM: ... block of stone, presumably set up to fall on your heads when you enter the inside.

Kenzo: And there's only one door in here?

DM: There's only one door into the temple, just the main door. Because you don't live to be as grand as you are-

Unknown: By trusting people.

DM: ... by trusting everyone.

Delwath: And I wanted to short rest, so I didn't want to scry again.

DM: Struggling to pull the giant block of stone up, but you didn't see the mechanism that he was trying to set.

DM: Okay, well this hap—this is all happening after the lynx came.

Unknown: Yeah.

DM: So maybe you didn't see it.

Delwath: Well, no, the lynx would have-

markers.reading: Another half hour of walking reaches the elven memorial beside the circular road.

evidence.quote:
DM: So you keep walking. After another, like half an hour of walking, you, you come to the point where the road curves and it seems to spiral, to join, um, like a circular road.

DM: And just where it joins this road that's circling up to the top of the mountain, um, you see, uh, again, on the edge of the path, a sort of a slight clearing where there's two unusually tall trees. And almost like growing between the trees there's this sort of curving piece of, uh, sort of pale gray stone, but it looks like... This actually sort of grows into the trees. And written on the stone are hundreds of names of elves written in Elvish. But the s- the, the scripts almost seem to like drift slowly through the stone between the two trees.

duration.basis: Narrated additional walk after the rest.

markers.reading: Touching the memorial reveals a remembered elf on battlements facing ships, then earlier memories of that elf’s life.

evidence.quote:
DM: So when you touch it, um, one of these like names kind of drifts towards your hand and you suddenly have a memor—a, you suddenly see a vision or a memory-

Kenzo: Mm.

DM: ... of, um, an elf standing in a rank of hundreds of elves, um, on a battlements watching a fleet of ships sailing on a sea. You don't recognize any of this. Um, and as they're, um, drawing their, like arrows, suddenly they all draw their arrows and suddenly like all of the arrows burst into flames immediately as they're released from the bows, and this rain of fire flies down on the ships.

DM: And then something flies up from one of the ships, like a, not a dragon, like some sort of twisted beast like the Nazgul creatures in The Lord of the Rings, right? And dives down and grabs this elf and like rips him-

DM: ... it seems like the, so the, the sort of magic of it is when you put your hand there, some names sort of drift towards you, right? Like the ones that maybe are the, the closest to you and you, you, you see back in this person's life and you see that they were originally, uh—they first joined the army as a quartermaster, and you see them cooking, right? You see like they were... You, you get a sort of reflection or echo of some of the things they left behind and the people that they, other elves and humans that they cared for.

Delwath: Any way of telling where they were born or grew up? Or-

DM: No.

Kenzo: But this is-

DM: Long ago and far away.

Kenzo: Yeah.

DM: But y- the sense, like the feeling you get is like this: your in—your intuition is that all of these are names of elves who died.

markers.reading: The forest shares a memory of pilgrims walking through its formerly more vibrant moonlit landscape.

evidence.quote:
Kenzo: Uh, and I, I basically tell it that I want to also remember it, and I'm saying it as, like, the... Like, and I—I'm asking for it to share back to me a memory or an image that I can put into the staff.

DM: You... Yeah, I get what you're going for. Um, so you, you see, you see an image of what must be long ago, the moon still shining, um, and people walking on the road. A- you know, everybody's, you know, carrying different things. Like, there's a couple elves, there's humans. Um, there's, like, one stoneborn. Like, it's not... It's a mixed species flock, right? Like, there's this just people traveling, and, and you do get the feel it—like you have a sort of vibe, right? It's not a clear image. It's more of a vibe. Yeah. It is mostly humans and elves, but...

DM: And everybody is remembered in different ways, right? The, the humans have their gods, the elves have their gods. But everywhere through the forest, everybody is remembered.

Kenzo: Hmm.

DM: And then, and you get the vibe of, like, the forest. Y- you know, it's vibrant, right? It's like, you know, the s—the moon is shining, but the leaves are sort of rustling. The f- flowers are blooming. There's... And it seems it's much more alive than it seems now. Like, the trees are fine, right, but there's-

Kenzo: Hmm.

DM: ... just less. Th- everything's duller-

Kenzo: Mm-hmm.
